paras: Acanthodactylus boueti, also known commonly as  Chabanaud's fringe-fingered lizard, is a species of lizard in the family Lacertidae. The species is native to West Africa.
The specific name, boueti, is in honor of French physician and ornithologist Georges Bouet (1869–1957), who worked in French West Africa in 1906–1930.
A. boueti is found in Benin, Ghana, Nigeria, and Togo.
The preferred natural habitat of A. boueti is savanna, at altitudes from sea level to 500 m (1,600 ft).
